User ran the live-booking-availability test suggested in the prior entry. Checked recreation.gov's per-day availability table directly (not just the summary calendar text) for two dates: (1) 4/21/2027 -- before both proposed seasons, so non-discriminating as expected -- Cottonwood Lakes and Cottonwood Pass both show a released value of 0 (confirmed no quota, not 'NR'). (2) 9/21-24/2026 -- inside the discriminating window (after Sep15, before Nov1) -- Cottonwood Lakes and Cottonwood Pass show 'NR' on all 4 days. Per the page's own legend, NR = 'Not Yet Released', a distinct status from 'Unavailable' -- it means the system hasn't opened booking for that date, not that the date is confirmed out of season. Critically, the SAME 4 dates for Deer Lakes (a plain John Muir Wilderness trail, general Inyo system) already show real released numbers (6, 6, NR, 6) one row below -- meaning the 6-month advance window is clearly already open system-wide for that date range, yet Cottonwood specifically has not released for it. This is strong (not fully conclusive, since NR could in principle still resolve to a nonzero number later) structural evidence that Cottonwood Lakes/Cottonwood Pass run on a DIFFERENT release/quota mechanism than standard JM-coded trails, consistent with -- and further supporting -- the shorter GT-specific season already adopted in permits.csv. Does not upgrade the resolution to full certainty, but adds a third independent data point (live booking system behavior, not just static documents) pointing the same direction as the two PDF sources.

First independent verification of this permit_group (previously web-search synthesis only). CORRECTS the reservation mechanism: the 60% portion was modeled as a simple rolling reservation window (like Inyo/SEKI); it's actually a WEEKLY LOTTERY -- each week-long hiking-start window gets its own application period (opens Sunday 12:01am, closes the following Saturday 11:59pm, ~24 weeks/168 days ahead, results by Monday 5pm), with lottery-unclaimed spots opening first-come the following Friday up to 3 days out, and the remaining 40% released 7 days out (up to 3 days before entry). Structurally closer to the Whitney Zone lottery than to Inyo's system, just weekly instead of annual. ALSO CORRECTS an implicit assumption: season start is NOT a fixed May 1 park-wide -- source states late-April starts are available 'in some -- but not all -- areas of the park', with exact per-area dates in a downloadable dataset (linked from the source page, not retrieved). 05-01 in this row is now flagged as an approximation, not confirmed. permits.py gained a Yosemite-specific status branch so the report says 'apply to the weekly lottery' instead of the generic 'book now', matching the Whitney/CPMA precedent for permits whose mechanism doesn't fit the generic rolling-reservation model.

DAY-USE PERMIT REQUIREMENT IS CONTESTED BETWEEN TWO OFFICIAL SOURCES. Eldorado NF's own day-use page states day use permits are available at trailheads only from the start of quota season through Sept 30, and that 'outside of these times no day use permits are needed'. recreation.gov's permit page states a wilderness permit is required for overnight camping AS WELL AS day visits, year-round; the official 2011 zone map says the same. This project currently asserts year-round, siding with two sources against the land manager's own page -- normally the land manager would win on a regulatory question, which is why this is logged rather than resolved. IMPORTANT PROVENANCE CAVEAT: the Eldorado NF text was read via a web-search snippet, not a direct page fetch (blocked from this environment), so it needs a first-hand read before being acted on. Do not silently flip the value on snippet evidence alone.

Eldorado NF's camping page states the California Campfire Permit requirement in full, and reading it exposed that this project had the rule WRONG in five places and inconsistent across seven. CORRECTS THE SCOPE: the permit covers campfires, stoves, LANTERNS and BARBEQUES -- five permit_groups described it as applying to a 'stove' alone. CORRECTS THE EXEMPTION: it is required outside a campground or RV *and in some developed campgrounds*, so 'outside a developed campground' was not a safe exemption as previously written. ADDS two facts held nowhere: the signer must be 18 or older (a group of minors cannot self-issue), and the legal basis is 36 CFR 261.52(k) / PRC 4433. URL CORRECTION: this project carried three different links for one permit (fs.usda.gov/main/r5/passes-permits on the 'none' group, readyforwildfire.org on gtw_free, nothing on the rest), and the Eldorado NF page itself cites 'www.preventwildfiresca.org', which does not resolve. The working path is readyforwildfire.org/prevent-wildfire/campfire-safety, which links through to the permit portal at permit.preventwildfiresca.org -- so gtw_free's link was the closest to right all along. STRUCTURAL FIX: because this is California state law rather than a per-wilderness rule, it is now stored once in data/regulations.csv scoped to the CA jurisdiction and inherited by every group, and the seven duplicated copies have been removed. ALSO ADDS an Eldorado NF-wide rule: dispersed camping outside a developed campground is capped at 10 days per ranger district per calendar year.

DELIBERATELY NOT CAPTURED: the Guest Reviews panel (842 reviews, 4.5 stars, 610/140/46/17/29 by star). It rates satisfaction with the permit and booking experience, not any fact about the wilderness, and nothing in it changes a trip plan. Neither open conflict on this group is touched by any of the above: the day-use season question and the 25-vs-30 ft Special Management Area setback both still need a first-hand read of the disputed source.
